title: Internet information on child oral health and the first dental visit
screen_reason: Content analysis of Google search results: 157 unique websites retrieved for four child-first-dental-visit (CFDV) keywords were coded against an external ground truth (international paediatric dental association guidelines: first visit at first tooth eruption or by age one) as 'similar to guidelines' vs 'dissimilar to guidelines'. Table 3 is headed 'accurate CDFV timings (and inaccurate CDFV timings)' and the paper labels the discordant advice 'misinformation'. This is guideline concordance stated as accurate/inaccurate against an external standard, so it is CONTENT (not QUALITY): a wholly correct site could not receive the 'dissimilar' label. A quantitative share with a denominator is available (25 of 157 unique sites).

estimates.country: Australia (Google searched under the Australian domain, location predetermined at Perth, Australia)
estimates.platform: Google search engine, Australian domain (http://www.google.com.au/), classic mode
estimates.date: 5 pm on 23 July 2011 until 10.30 am on 24 July 2011
estimates.measure_type: % of unique websites retrieved by CFDV searches that recommended a timing for the child's first dental visit inconsistent with international paediatric guidelines
estimates.denominator: 157 unique websites remaining after removing 43 duplicates from the top-50 Google.com.au results for each of four CFDV search terms (200 results)
estimates.definition: The site stated a recommended timing for a child's first dental visit that was 'dissimilar to guidelines', i.e. not from first tooth eruption (about six months) to one year of age; the discordant sites suggested an age range of 2 to 3.5 years. Sites that did not mention CFDV timing at all (n = 55) count in the denominator but not the numerator.
estimates.misinfo_def: "International paediatric guidelines suggest the first dental visit should take place as soon as the first tooth erupts and/or by the age of one year." Sites departing from this are described by the authors as 'misinformation' and, in Table 3, as 'inaccurate CDFV timings'.
estimates.source_quote: Similar to guidelines 77 15 6 30 26 Dissimilar to guidelines 25 0 0 17 8 Total contributing entries 157 40 (25.5%) 117 (74.5%)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The authors themselves compared each retrieved site's stated CFDV timing with the timing recommended by seven professional dental associations / international paediatric guidelines (AAPD, ADA, BSPD, IAPD; Table 2). No inter-coder reliability, no blinding and no second coder are reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: By using selected search terms (Table 1), online information regarding the CFDV was searched via the Google search engine under the Australian domain (location predetermined at Perth, Australia; classic mode, URL: http://www.google.com.au/) from 5 pm on 23 July 2011 until 10.30 am on 24 July 2011. The first 50 search results for each of the selected search terms were compiled and analysed for the type of site and the timing recommended for CFDV.
estimates.notes: The 15.9% is an exact part/whole share from two verbatim counts in Table 4 with the same denominator (25 dissimilar sites out of 157 total contributing entries), per R8. The narrower denominator 'sites that mentioned a CFDV timing' (77 + 25 = 102) was NOT used because 102 is a cross-category sum the paper never states. Topic is child oral health, coded health_other. The unit is a website reached through search, hence url and denom_selection=curated (rank-truncated top-50 sets).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Private-site subgroup: "In contrast, two-thirds (n = 81) of private sites recommended timing for CFDV but approximately one-third (n = 25) reported inconsistent guidelines suggesting an age range of 2 to 3.5 years (Table 4)" — 25/81 = 30.9% of private sites that gave a timing. Not extracted as a separate row because it is the same country x platform x measure with a subset denominator (site ownership type), not a distinct estimate; the pooled 157-site figure is the representative point. (2) Per-search-term figures in Table 3 (e.g. 'child first dental visit' 36 accurate / 4 inaccurate) are not extracted: the four keyword sets overlap (43 duplicates) and the four sets are the same country, platform and measure. (3) Accuracy-side percentages that would need a complement I computed are excluded by R8: 'only 28.6% of all authoritative sites provided readily accessible guidelines ... consistent with international paediatric guidelines'; 'public sites had a higher accuracy of recommended timing for CFDV (100%) compared to private sites (69%)'; 'only 44% of those sites reported guidelines consistent with those recommended' (68 dental-professional-owned sites). (4) Ranges quoted in the Discussion ('Depending on the search terms used, this study suggested that timing for CFDV on the internet was available for 40-82% of search results. When the accuracy of information was assessed, 24-72% of sites providing such information were considered accurate') are ranges over search terms of the accurate share, not a point misinformation estimate.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of Google.com.au search results, four purposive CFDV keywords, top 50 results each (200 results; 43 duplicates removed leaving 157 unique sites), searched over 17 hours on 23-24 July 2011 from a fixed location (Perth). Sites classified by ownership type (organization, government, dental professional, non-dental professional) and by whether the recommended CFDV timing was absent, similar to, or dissimilar to international paediatric guidelines. No sampling of non-Google engines, no inter-coder reliability statistics, no blinding, no second rater, and the authors note non-reproducibility due to search fluidity and location-tailored results.
rob.item6_quote: International paediatric guidelines suggest the first dental visit should take place as soon as the first tooth erupts and/or by the age of one year.
rob.item10_quote: Forty-three duplicates were found in 200 search results (across the four phrases), leaving 157 unique sites.
